extraction.name: SeamlessM4T
extraction.description: A single model that supports speech-to-speech translation, speech-to-text translation, text-to-speech translation, text-to-text translation, and automatic speech recognition for up to 100 languages.
extraction.creator: Seamless Communication, Loïc Barrault, Yu-An Chung, Mariano Coria Meglioli, David Dale, Ning Dong, Paul-Ambroise Duquenne, Hady Elsahar, Hongyu Gong, Kevin Heffeman, John Hoffman, Christopher Klaiber, Pengwei Li, Daniel Licht, Jean Maillard, Alice Rakotoarison, Kaushik Ram Sadagopan, Guillaume Wenzek, Ethan Ye, Bapi Akula, Peng-Jen Chen, Naji El Hachem, Brian Ellis, Gabriel Mejia Gonzalez, Justin Haaheim, Prangthip Hansanti, Russ Howes, Bemie Huang, Min-Jae Hwang, Hirofumi Inaguma, Somya Jain, Elahe Kalbassi, Amanda Kallet, Ilia Kulikov, Janice Lam, Daniel Li, Xutai Ma, Ruslan Mavlyutov, Benjamin Peloquin, Mohamed Ramadan, Abinesh Ramakrishnan, Anna Sun, Kevin Tran, Tuan Tran, Igor Tufanov, Vish Vogeti, Carleigh Wood, Yilin Yang, Bokai Yu, Pierre Andrews, Can Balioglu, Marta R. Costa-jussà, Onur Celebi, Maha Elbayad, Cynthia Gao, Francisco Guzmán, Justine Kao, Ann Lee, Alexandre Mourachko, Juan Pino, Sravya Popuri, Christophe Ropers, Safiyyah Saleem, Holger Schwenk, Paden Tomasello, Changhan Wang, Jeff Wang, Skyler Wang (Meta AI, INRIA, UC Berkeley)
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Created a multimodal corpus of automatically aligned speech translations by chunking raw audio files into overlapping segments, applying speech Language Identification (LID), and projecting speech and text corpora into a common embedding space to find parallel instances.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Some samples from the evaluation data were missing (in 8 out of 21 languages: Catalan, German, Estonian, French, Italian, Mongolian, Persian, and Portuguese).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 4 million hours of raw audio originating from a publicly available repository of crawled web data.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Audio files were deduplicated, downloaded, and resampled at 16KHz. Non-speech data was filtered out using an audio event detection (AED) model. Audio files were also split into shorter segments using a Voice Activity Detection (VAD) model, and several possible overlapping splits were created (over-segmentation).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Deduplicated audio file URLs, downloaded and resampled at 16KHz, filtered out non-speech data with an audio event detection model, and applied voice activity detection to split audio files into shorter segments.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators examined source-target audio or audio-text pairs and evaluated the item for semantic similarity using the XSTS protocol or evaluated naturalness using the MOS protocol.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: In cases of disagreement of score values of 2 or more, 2 additional annotators evaluated the item, and the median score was taken.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Aims to facilitate multilingual contact and bridge the translation gap between high and low-resource languages, promoting inclusion and accessibility.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The model overgeneralizes to masculine forms when translating from neutral terms and shows a lack of robustness when varying gender.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Wordlist-based toxicity detection techniques produce false positives due to tokenization issues and context-dependent toxicity. The model also suffers from truncations and omissions in longer source audios for S2ST.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, inference, and fine-tuning for speech-to-speech, speech-to-text, text-to-speech, text-to-text translation, and automatic speech recognition.

name.evidence: SeamlessM4T: Massively Multilingual & Multimodal Machine Translation

description.evidence: we introduce SeamlessM4T —Massively Multilingual & Multimodal MachineTranslation—a single model that supports speechto-speech translation, speech-to-text translation, text-to-speech translation, text-to-text translation, and automatic speech recognition for up to 100 languages.

creator.evidence: Seamless Communication, Loïc Barrault∗, Yu-An Chung∗... Meta AI,‡INRIA,§UC Berkeley

inLanguage.evidence: automatic speech recognition for up to 100 languages.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: we created a multimodal corpus of automatically aligned speech translations of more than 470,000 hours, dubbed SeamlessAlign... Starting with a large collection of raw audio, we chunked files into overlapping segments and applied speech Language Identification (LID)... Speech and text corpora were then projected into a common embedding space, in which mining was performed to identify translation pairs

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: We start with 4 million hours of raw audio originating from a publicly available repository of crawled web data.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: We start with 4 million hours of raw audio originating from a publicly available repository of crawled web data.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: we deduplicated the audio file URLs found in the repository, downloaded the audio files, and resampled at 16KHz. Subsequently, we filtered out the non-speech data with a bespoke audio event detection (AED) model... First, we used an open Voice Activity Detection (VAD) model [Silero, 2021] to split audio files into shorter segments.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: During annotation, 3 annotators examined each source-target audio pair (or audio-text pair) and evaluated the item for semantic similarity using the XSTS protocol... To evaluate and compare generated speech quality for the S2ST task, we used a standard Mean Opinion Score (MOS) protocol to evaluate naturalness, quality of sound, and clarity of speech

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: In cases where the 3 annotators had a disagreement of score values of 2 or more, 2 additional annotators evaluated the same item again, bringing the total to 5 evaluator scores for those items. The median score over annotators of the same audio pair was then taken for each evaluation sentence pair

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: 3 annotators examined each source-target audio pair

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: we resort to pseudo-labeling the ASR data with a multilingual T2TT model. In this case, we used NLLB-200-3.3B

rai:personalSensitiveInformation.evidence: When possible, these pairings were made to match user gender (53% of the time over the entirety of the Fleurs test partition

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: an increasingly interconnected world calls for the development of technologies that can facilitate and streamline multilingual contact both online and offline... our effort seeks to bridge the translation gap between those who speak high and low-resource languages.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: SeamlessM4T overgeneralizes to masculine forms when translating from neutral terms (with an average preference of ∼10%) while showing a lack of robustness when varying gender by an amount of ∼3%.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: wordlist-based toxicity detection techniques are known to produce a substantial number of false positives. These are typically due to one of two main factors: tokenization issues and toxicity list items that are only toxic in certain contexts... longer source audios may more likely to suffer from truncations and omissions in the target audio.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: all contributions in this work—including models, inference code, finetuning recipes backed by our improved modeling toolkit Fairseq2 , and metadata to recreate the unfiltered 470,000 hours of SeamlessAlign —are open-sourced
